items.title: CVE-2026-117349 - Slow unbounded memory growth on paused pre-BIP31 peers
items.desc: Bitcoin Core queues announcements for all peers, including paused ones. Pre-BIP31 peers could stay paused forever and let the queue grow unboundedly. A fix for this issue was released in Bitcoin Core versions 29.5, 30.4, 31.2 and 32.1. This issue is considered Medium severity and easily discoverable. Details Bitcoin Core implements backpressure for slow to read peers. Once the queue of messages to send a peer grows past a certain limit, it will mark that peer as paused for send purposes. However, it will still add some announcements to the queue, in particular the frequent transaction INVs. This is normally not an issue, as peers which don’t respond to a (nonced) ping message within 20 minutes get disconnected. However, this disconnection is not enabled for peers that don’t support BIP 31 nonced ping messages. Therefore, a malicious peer could pretend to not support those and strategically delay reading messages to cause the queue to slowly grow without limit. Memory usage could grow at a rate of up to 2MB per hour per inbound peer, and 5MB per hour per outbound peer. Nodes running with -blocksonly are much less affected, as transaction announcements make up the bulk of the queued messages. Attribution This issue was discovered through an automated LLM scan, as part of Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral. The Loupe finding was validated and surfaced to the Bitcoin Core team by Gregory Sanders. This issue was independently re-discovered by L0rinc. Timeline 2026-09-15 Project Loupe identifies the issue and notifies Greg Sanders, who validates the report and notifies the Bitcoin Core security team on the same day. 2026-09-21 L0rinc privately notifies Gregory Sanders, who replies that issue was already reported. 2026-10-26 Antoine Poinsot opens PR #36667 to mitigate the vulnerability. 2026-10-26 PR #36667 is merged and backported to versions 29, 30, 31, and 32. 2026-10-27 Bitcoin Core 31.2 and 32.1 are released with a fix 2026-10-28 Bitcoin Core 29.5, 30.4 are released with a fix 2026-10-28 Public disclosure.

items.title: CVE-2026-117350 - Unbounded memory growth through TCP urgent data on non-Linux systems
items.desc: On platforms other than Linux, a malicious peer could cause a node to run out of memory by sending TCP urgent (out-of-band) data. A fix for this issue was released in Bitcoin Core versions 29.5, 30.4, 31.2 and 32.1. This issue is considered Medium severity and easily discoverable. Details Bitcoin Core uses a different backend (based on select()) to monitor socket events on platforms other than Linux (where it uses poll()). This issue only affects the select() code path. Bitcoin Core users on Linux are therefore not affected by this issue. Bitcoin Core limits the amount of data it will queue for processing per peer, by temporarily pausing reads when the queue exceeds a certain size. The select() socket monitoring backend watched sockets for exceptional conditions regardless of whether reads were paused. In handling that event, a read on the socket would be triggered, which could queue up more data for processing for that peer, without limit. That event can be triggered by sending TCP urgent data. This allows a paused peer to bypass the backpressure mechanism and queue an unbounded amount of data for processing. In practice, this means a malicious peer can trivially crash any Windows, macOS or BSD node it is connected to. Attribution This issue was discovered through an automated LLM scan, as part of Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral. The Loupe finding was validated and surfaced to the Bitcoin Core team by Gregory Sanders. Timeline 2026-10-23 Project Loupe identifies the issue and notifies Greg Sanders, who validates the report and notifies the Bitcoin Core security team on the same day. 2026-10-26 Antoine Poinsot opens PR #36665 to fix this issue. 2026-10-26 PR #36665 is merged and backported to versions 29, 30, 31, and 32. 2026-10-27 Bitcoin Core 31.2 and 32.1 are released with a fix 2026-10-28 Bitcoin Core 29.5, 30.4 are released with a fix 2026-10-28 Public disclosure.
